entries.claim: A released cube can descend over the BinFill opening and then cease to be visible while the bin interior still looks black. A later apparently empty interior alone is insufficient evidence of a missed deposit or justification to add another cube.
entries.conditions: When placement is ambiguous, review sparse-to-dense release history to distinguish the held cube's descent into the opening from separately appearing tabletop cubes. In the evidenced episode, the observed descent/disappearance was followed by official success after pressing stop, without another pickup. This does not establish hidden bin mechanics, a universal disappearance rule, or success from disappearance alone.

entries.claim: For a green-cube pickup whose final approach places an adjacent non-target cube near a finger, do not carry a full-phase duration authorization through closure without review. In the evidenced run, an unguarded100-control authorization from0 reached clear neighboring-cube displacement at86 and target escape by89 before the wake at100; the attempted lift left the target on the table. Prefer a before-command gripper-change wake during approach, then close visual review of final alignment, closure and initial lift using a single candidate prefix.
entries.conditions: Conditional on crowded final descent/closure or visible finger encroachment near another cube, not ordinary clear-space approach. Earliest clear displacement was86 (offset86); exact first contact is uncertain. The proposed16-control review interval is conservative advice, not an experimentally established safe bound. The before-command guard observes the commanded closure transition only, not collision or escape; use current RGB to assess alignment and verify actual carriage. Do not infer grasp from aperture alone.

entries.claim: Separate ordinary BinFill button approach from final near-button descent. A full-phase90-control authorization included an unactivated down/up attempt and retreat before the next review. Once near contact, prefer a single candidate prefix to check measured progress and official feedback before allowing continued withdrawal or choosing bounded correction.
entries.conditions: Applies to final button descent/possible contact, not clear-space approach. In the evidenced authorization204-294, lowest visible approach was around285-286 and clear retreat by287 (offset83); exact contact and earliest inadequate depth are not established. No success at294; a bounded vertical correction was followed by official success315. This does not prove correction was necessary, truncation caused the miss, or any fixed depth/prefix is universally safe.16-control advice is a conservative review interval, not a validated safety bound. General button-motion-not-activation already covers epistemic caution; this entry adds only phase-specific scheduling advice.
entries.phase: button final descent and activation verification

entries.claim: For BinFill placement with uncertain held-cube alignment over the opening, review before commanded opening rather than relying on an after-measured gripper-change wake. A60-control placement authorization woke after48 controls only after the cube had been released outside the near rim and landed on the table. Prefer an explicit before-command gripper-change guard during transport, then close visual review of final alignment and a single candidate prefix for release.
entries.conditions: Conditional on near-bin placement/release with uncertain alignment, including an off-center grasp after recovery; not a reason to shorten all clear-space transport. In authorization780-828, dense818-828 and original823 wrist show release822, earliest clear outside-opening descent823 (offset43), tabletop miss824 (offset44), before the after-measured wake828. Exact earliest pre-release alignment error is unknown. The before-command guard observes a command transition, not alignment or collision. Suggested16-control review is conservative advice, not a validated safe bound; use a shorter prefix if current visual/FK risk warrants.
